claims.text: たぬき蕎麦のトッピングである天かす（揚げ玉）は小麦粉の天ぷらバッターと同じ油で揚げられており、グルテン交差汚染のリスクが高い。
そばつゆには通常の醤油（小麦含有）が使用されており、GF対応の代替醤油の情報は確認されていない。
だしは和風出汁（鰹節ベースと推定）であり、植物性ブロスの提供は確認されていない。肉そばメニューも存在する。

All noodles (kishimen, udon, soba) are wheat-based and cooked in the same kitchen. Tempura, tonkatsu, karaage, and other breaded items are also on the menu, making wheat cross-contamination near-certain throughout the kitchen.

The kitchen uses tamari soy sauce (たまり醤油) as its primary seasoning, which is traditionally wheat-reduced compared to standard shoyu, but no gluten-free certification is claimed and standard soy sauce use cannot be ruled out for all dishes.
The dashi base is muro-bushi (fish-derived), used throughout the noodle broths. No vegan broth alternative is offered. Shared cooking equipment with meat, seafood, and egg dishes throughout.

No allergy-handling information or allergy menu is mentioned on the official website or Tabelog listing. The restaurant does not appear to cater to dietary restrictions; diners with serious allergies should call ahead (052-571-0485).
Use of tamari soy sauce (たまり醤油) rather than standard wheat-heavy shoyu is a notable ingredient choice, though it does not make the restaurant gluten-free.
Tempura and breaded katsu are prepared in the same kitchen. No separate fryer or preparation area for gluten-free orders is mentioned anywhere in available sources.
Dishes use a house-blend soy sauce (自家製醤油) for items like the chicken katsu bowl; conventional Japanese soy sauce contains wheat. No tamari or gluten-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned.
Broths are described as using bonito-based dashi (かつお出汁). Tempura and dashi-maki tamago (egg) are prominent menu items, making a plant-free meal unlikely without special arrangement.

No allergen menu, allergy protocol, or staff training for dietary restrictions is noted in any available source. The restaurant operates without credit card machines and with a chalkboard-only menu, suggesting a basic neighbourhood setup without formal allergen systems.
The young owner is consistently described as approachable and communicative — a direct phone call (052-524-6555) ahead of a visit is the most practical path for anyone with dietary needs.

name: めん処　幸の家 (Mendokoro Yukino-ya)

claims.text: All noodle dishes use wheat-based udon or kishimen noodles; the miso broth almost certainly contains wheat-based miso and standard soy sauce. No wheat-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned.
Broth bases are traditional Japanese style; katsuobushi (bonito) or pork-derived dashi is standard in miso-nikomi preparations. No plant-based broth option is documented.

name: めしや ばさらび (Meshiya Basarabi)

claims.text: 醤油タレや煮物に小麦入り醤油が使用されている可能性が高い。グルテンフリー醤油の使用に関する情報は公開されていない。
鰹・昆布ベースのだしが調理全般に使われていると推定され、植物性食材の料理にも動物性だしが入る可能性がある。
炭火焼き素材（魚・肉・野菜）は焼くだけの調理も多く、タレや調味料を別出しで依頼できる可能性がある。来店前の電話確認を推奨。

name: メゼス サントリーニ (Mezes Santorini)

claims.text: No information on kitchen cross-contamination practices was found in any source. The kitchen appears small (30-seat restaurant in a converted townhouse), raising the likelihood of shared surfaces.

Greek cuisine does not use soy sauce or dashi as base ingredients, which eliminates the most common Japanese gluten/hidden-fish vectors. However, wheat flour is used in béchamel (moussaka) and likely in Greek pies.
Charcoal grill is used for both meat and seafood; no separation from plant-based items confirmed. Dairy (feta, yogurt, béchamel) is central to the menu.
No source mentions any allergy-handling policy, allergen menu, or staff training for dietary restrictions. English communication is noted as possible with the Greek owner.
Greek cuisine base avoids soy sauce, mirin, dashi, and other umami seasonings standard in Japanese kitchens, making it structurally safer from several common hidden-gluten and hidden-fish sources.
Olive-oil-based cooking and fresh vegetable/seafood focus means some dishes (marinated octopus, grilled fish, salads) may be naturally GF — but this must be verified per dish.
グルテンフリー対応や交差汚染への取り組みについて公式・口コミ上での言及はなく、詳細は不明。事前の電話確認が必須。
もつ鍋の自家製たれに醤油ベースの酢だれを使用。一般的な醤油には小麦が含まれるため、セリアック病や小麦アレルギーの方は要注意。グルテンフリー醤油使用の記載なし。
もつ鍋専門店であり、全メニューが動物性食材を使用。ビーガン・ベジタリアン向けの選択肢および交差汚染への配慮についての情報はない。
アレルギー対応や食事制限への配慮に関する記載はウェブ上に見当たらない。来店前に電話（052-961-9525）で確認することを強く推奨。
No information available on cross-contamination controls. The kitchen handles wheat-containing soy sauce, champon noodles, and likely other wheat-based ingredients throughout service.
Motsusuki is a sukiyaki-style dish whose sauce is almost certainly soy-sauce-based (containing wheat). No gluten-free soy sauce (tamari) alternative is mentioned anywhere in listings or reviews.
The finish course is champon noodles, which contain wheat.
Entire menu is built around beef offal — no plant-based dishes exist; vegan cross-contact is moot as there is nothing vegan to order.
No allergy-handling policy or allergen menu is referenced in any source. Diners with dietary restrictions should call 052-571-2919 before visiting.
